(a) THE RING (source 1888-1889 "nonzero Laurent polynomial f in a with coefficients in the integral domain ℤ[z^{±1}]"; 1892 "nonzero element of ℤ[a^{±1},z^{±1}]"). Lean: f : R with R = Laurent₂ ℤ = AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ (ℤ × ℤ) (LinkLaurentRing.lean 71, 76); Mathlib's AddMonoidAlgebra is a one-field structure `coeff : (ℤ×ℤ) →₀ ℤ` (Defs.lean 64-69), `single m r = ofCoeff (Finsupp.single m r)` (Defs.lean 222). The source itself uses both views of one object ("the same symbols with the subscript z" applied to elements of ℤ[a^{±1},z^{±1}]), so identifying (ℤ[z^{±1}])[a^{±1}] with ℤ[a^{±1},z^{±1}] is the source's own reading; the canonical isomorphism sends a^d z^k to single (d,k) 1 and the a^d-coefficient c_d(z) ∈ ℤ[z^{±1}] to the row k ↦ coeffAt d k f, so "c_d ≠ 0" is exactly "∃ k, coeffAt d k f ≠ 0" — which is precisely the quantifier shape used in the degA/mindegA clauses (statement 38-39, 44-45). The identification is pinned by field `monomial` (statement 28): single (d,k) 1 = (aUnit^d * zUnit^k : Rˣ) for all d k : ℤ, with R.aUnit = monoUnit (1,0) = ⟨single (1,0) 1, single (-1,0) 1,…⟩ and R.zUnit = monoUnit (0,1) (LinkLaurentRing 126-127, 168, 170), so (d,k) ↦ a^d z^k with a in the first slot and z in the second, negative exponents via the unit inverses — matching def:C's "[a^{d_Q} z^0]" order (1692). Faithful. Field `domain` (statement 26): IsDomain R. The printed words are "the integral domain ℤ[z^{±1}]" — a property of the coefficient ring, which has no separate Lean type under the adopted reading. IsDomain R implies the subring ℤ[z^{±1}] is a domain and is mathematically equivalent to it (Laurent polynomials over a domain form a domain); it is a true statement (Mathlib NoZeroDivisors.lean instances via UniqueSums (ℤ×ℤ), Prod.instUniqueSums; `example : IsDomain R := inferInstance` at LinkLaurentRing 104). It is recorded below as STRONGER than the printed clause (asserted of the whole ring rather than of the coefficient subring), not as a fidelity break; the docstring (statement 24-25) states the intended reading correctly.

(b) COEFFICIENT (def:C 1692-1694 "the coefficient of a^{d_Q} z^0 (zero if that monomial is absent)"). coeffAt d k f := f.coeff (d,k) (LinkLaurentRing 286) is the Finsupp evaluation, i.e. literally the coefficient. Field `coeff` (statement 31-33): (i) on single (p,q) c the value is c if (p,q)=(d,k) else 0 — value on monomials incl. "zero if absent"; (ii) coefficient-wise equal elements are equal — coefficients determine f. Both are true of the primitive and pin the intended reading. The bundle does not additionally state additivity of coeffAt or single (p,q) c = c • a^p z^q, but since coeffAt is a transparent one-line definition on Mathlib's coefficient function this is not a gap in fidelity (noted, not a discrepancy).

(c) deg_a, mindeg_a (source 1889-1891 "deg_a f = maxdeg_a f denotes the largest a-exponent with nonzero coefficient and mindeg_a f the smallest; both are integers"). Lean degA f := f.supDegree wtA (LinkLaurentRing 392) = f.coeff.support.sup (fun e => (e.1 : WithBot ℤ)) (Mathlib Degree.lean 254-255; wtA at 371); degAZ f := (degA f).unbotD 0 (446; WithBot.lean 81-82). Field `degA` (statement 36-39), for f ≠ 0: degA f = ↑(degAZ f) [WithBot value is a genuine integer: "both are integers"]; ∃ k, coeffAt (degAZ f) k f ≠ 0 [the a^{degAZ f}-coefficient in ℤ[z^{±1}] is nonzero: attained]; ∀ d k, coeffAt d k f ≠ 0 → d ≤ degAZ f [bounds every a-exponent with nonzero coefficient: largest]; and the uniqueness conjunct (any attained upper bound equals degAZ f), which is a consequence of the previous two and adds nothing beyond "denotes the largest". Field `mindegA` (statement 42-45) is the exact dual with mindegA f := f.infDegree wtA' (396; Degree.lean 624-625), mindegAZ := untopD 0 (506), WithTop, ≤ reversed. Faithful. `maxdeg_a`: the source declares it a synonym ("deg_a f = maxdeg_a f"); the Lean renders both by the single term degA/degAZ (docstring statement 13); no separate identifier `maxdegA` exists, which is the natural rendering of a synonym — GLOSSARY should map maxdeg_a to degA/degAZ.

(d) deg_z, mindeg_z (source 1891-1893). Fields `degZ`, `mindegZ` (statement 47-50, 52-55) have the same four-conjunct shape with the roles of d and k swapped: degZ f := f.supDegree wtZ (400, wtZ = snd at 375), degZZ := unbotD 0 (560); mindegZ := infDegree wtZ' (403), mindegZZ := untopD 0 (607). "z-exponent with nonzero coefficient" is rendered ∃ d, coeffAt d k f ≠ 0, the right reading for an element of ℤ[a^{±1},z^{±1}]. Faithful.

f = 0: every degree clause is guarded by f ≠ 0 (statement 36, 42, 47, 52); `domain`, `monomial`, `coeff` say nothing about degrees. The conventions degAZ 0 = 0 etc. live only in the definitions (unbotD 0 / untopD 0) and no clause of the bundle asserts anything about them. (a) RING AND NONZERO f. Source 1888-1889: "a nonzero Laurent polynomial f in a with coefficients in the integral domain ℤ[z^{±1}]", i.e. f ∈ (ℤ[z^{±1}])[a^{±1}], f ≠ 0. Lean: f : R with R = Laurent₂ ℤ = AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ (ℤ × ℤ) (LinkLaurentRing.lean:71,76), exponent (d,k) ↦ a^d z^k pinned by field `monomial` (S:28), which expands via R.aUnit = monoUnit (1,0), R.zUnit = monoUnit (0,1) (LinkLaurentRing.lean:126-127,168,170) to single (d,k) 1 = (a^d z^k as units). The identification (ℤ[z^{±1}])[a^{±1}] ≅ ℤ[a^{±1},z^{±1}] is the standard iterated-Laurent isomorphism; under it "the coefficient of a^d is nonzero in ℤ[z^{±1}]" is exactly "∃ k, [a^d z^k] f ≠ 0", which is what every Lean attainment clause uses. Every degree field is guarded by `f ≠ 0 →` (S:36,42,47,52), matching "nonzero". Field `domain : IsDomain R` (S:26) renders "the integral domain ℤ[z^{±1}]" at the level of the whole ring R rather than the coefficient subring; it implies the printed attribute (a subring of a domain is a domain) and is true, but is stronger than what is printed — recorded under stronger_than_source; it does not touch the degree definitions.

(b) COEFFICIENT. Source: "nonzero coefficient" (1890), with def:C 1692-1694 fixing "[a^d z^k] … the coefficient of a^d z^k (zero if that monomial is absent)". Lean: coeffAt d k f := f.coeff (d,k) (LinkLaurentRing.lean:286), i.e. Finsupp evaluation of the AddMonoidAlgebra coefficient function (Mathlib Defs.lean:64-69) — this is literally "the coefficient, zero if absent". Field `coeff` (S:31-33) additionally pins the value on monomials (agrees with Finsupp.single_apply, Mathlib Defs.lean:222,225) and that coefficients determine f. Faithful.

(c) deg_a AND mindeg_a. Source 1889-1891: deg_a f = maxdeg_a f is the largest a-exponent with nonzero coefficient, mindeg_a f the smallest, both integers. Lean degA f = f.supDegree wtA = f.coeff.support.sup (fun e => ↑e.1) : WithBot ℤ (LinkLaurentRing.lean:371,392; Mathlib Degree.lean:254-255), degAZ f = (degA f).unbotD 0 (LinkLaurentRing.lean:446; Mathlib WithBot.lean:81-82); mindegA f = f.infDegree wtA' : WithTop ℤ (LinkLaurentRing.lean:373,396; Degree.lean:624-625), mindegAZ f = (mindegA f).untopD 0 (LinkLaurentRing.lean:506). Field `mindegA` (S:42-45) is the exact dual with mindegAZ f ≤ d and WithTop. Inequality directions and argument positions verified. Faithful.

Lean degZ = supDegree wtZ (weight e.2), degZZ = unbotD 0; mindegZ = infDegree wtZ', mindegZZ = untopD 0 (LinkLaurentRing.lean:375,377,400,403,560,607). refuters.argument: After a genuine search I found no nonzero f in ZZ[a^{+-1}, z^{+-1}] (under either reading of "coefficient") on which the printed deg_a / mindeg_a / deg_z / mindeg_z and the Lean degAZ / mindegAZ / degZZ / mindegZZ differ, and no printed clause without a Lean counterpart. Reason: write f = sum c_{d,k} a^d z^k (finite support, unique representation). Read as a Laurent polynomial in a over ZZ[z^{+-1}], its a^d-coefficient is c_d(z) = sum_k c_{d,k} z^k, and c_d != 0 in ZZ[z^{+-1}] iff exists k with c_{d,k} != 0 iff exists k with coeffAt d k f != 0 (coeffAt d k f := f.coeff (d,k), LinkLaurentRing.lean:286; AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff of single is Finsupp.single). Hence the printed "largest a-exponent with nonzero coefficient" is max{d : exists k, coeffAt d k f != 0}, which is exactly what the Lean degA clause (statement lines 36-39) asserts: degAZ f is attained (exists k, coeffAt (degAZ f) k f != 0), bounds every exponent with nonzero coefficient (forall d k, coeffAt d k f != 0 -> d <= degAZ f), and is the unique such integer. Symmetrically for mindegA (lines 42-45) and for the z-subscript degZ/mindegZ (lines 47-55), where the source already works in ZZ[a^{+-1},z^{+-1}] directly. The alternative reading of "coefficient" as the ZZ-coefficient of a^d z^k gives the same set {d : exists k, c_{d,k} != 0}, so both readings agree. Under the hood, Link.degA f = f.supDegree wtA = f.coeff.support.sup (fun e => (e.1 : WithBot ZZ)) (Mathlib: abbrev supDegree f := f.coeff.support.sup D); WithBot ZZ is linearly ordered so sup = max; degAZ f = (degA f).unbotD 0 and unbotD_coe : unbotD d (x : WithBot) = x, so for f != 0 (support nonempty, degA f != bot) degAZ f is the max first coordinate of the support. infDegree/untopD are the dual. Concrete checks: f = a^2 z^{-1} + a^2 z^3 - 1 has c_2 = z^{-1}+z^3, c_0 = -1, printed (deg_a, mindeg_a, deg_z, mindeg_z) = (2,0,3,-1); Lean support {(2,-1),(2,3),(0,0)} gives (2,0,3,-1). f = 5 a^{-3} z^4 - 7 z^{-2} gives (-3,0,4,-2) both ways. "Both are integers" is rendered by degAZ f : ZZ together with Link.degA f = (degAZ f : WithBot ZZ) (so not bot). "Nonzero" is the guard f != 0 on all four degree clauses; no clause says anything at f = 0 (the degAZ 0 = 0 convention of LinkLaurentRing.lean:446 is not in the bundle; domain/monomial/coeff mention no degree). The identification of (ZZ[z^{+-1}])[a^{+-1}] with R = AddMonoidAlgebra ZZ (ZZ x ZZ) is the standard ring isomorphism and the a-exponent of c a^d z^k is d on both sides, so the design reading is faithful for this definition. The monomial clause (line 28: single (d,k) 1 = aUnit^d * zUnit^k; true by monoUnit_zpow/monoUnit_mul) and the coeff clause (lines 31-33: Kronecker value on monomials, extensionality) are notation glue fixing what "a-exponent", "z-exponent" and "coefficient (zero if that monomial is absent)" denote; they add no content beyond that. Points where the Lean is STRONGER than or differs cosmetically from the source, none of which changes the defined objects and none of which I judge a refuting discrepancy: (1) domain : IsDomain R (line 26) asserts the whole ring ZZ[a^{+-1},z^{+-1}] is a domain, while the source says "coefficients in the integral domain ZZ[z^{+-1}]" (a property of the coefficient subring); the Lean clause implies the printed one (nontrivial subring of a domain is a domain) and is a true Mathlib instance (IsDomain R[A] from IsDomain ZZ, IsCancelAdd ZZ, UniqueSums (ZZ x ZZ)), but it is not literally the printed statement. (2) The synonym "deg_a f = maxdeg_a f" has no Lean declaration; it is rendered only in the module docstring (line 13, "deg_a f = maxdeg_a f is degAZ f"); since the source treats maxdeg_a as the same symbol, one Lean name suffices, but GLOSSARY should map maxdeg_a -> degAZ. (3) The fourth conjunct (uniqueness) in each degree clause is a redundant consequence of attainment + bound (harmless). Nothing WEAKER than the source was found.
